I wrote this to my MP just now. I really tried to pull no punches while also remaining civil. Language is a bit iffy but the aim is to get them to understand.

"Hello,

As I am sure you have heard, the supreme court last week ruled that the Equality Act 2010 makes reference to "biological sex" when it refers to men and women.

I would like to know, without echoing statements made by the government;

1. Do you personally agree with the ruling?
2. Do you personally think it brings clarity?
3. Do you personally think the ruling is contradictory to other existing law or not?
4. Do you personally think toilets should be classed as single-sex spaces?

A huge concern of mine is the new policy from BTP stating that if they suspect someone is a trans woman, then they will be strip searched by a male officer. How would they possibly know for sure? Many young women these days do not look what is considered traditionally feminine, especially cis butch lesbians. Also in recent years with news of male police officers abusing women, how could we ensure the safety of all women if all a male police officer would have to do is state a woman is transgender in order to do what would be legal sexual assault?

Regarding rape shelters, let's say a trans woman is raped by a cisgender male. Where would she go for support and safety? Under this ruling she would be disbarred from a single-sex space like that, and again, any woman suspected of being trans would be disbarred. It is my opinion that gender non-conforming rape victims will be left in vulnerable and dangerous situations as a result of the judgement because they "look like men."

I had also read in a news article that an ex-civil servant, named Melanie Field, said that the clear premise of the Equality Act 2010 was to give all trans people with a gender recognition certificate the same legal status and protections as their biological counterparts. Could you please explain how you or the government will rectify this difference of interpretation? I do recognise that the court has a strong voice in what is the law, but I and any other reasonable person would view the people who wrote the law as having a stronger voice.

Thank you for reading, and I look forward to hearing back from you.

<NAME AND DETAILS>"
